title: Targeting mitochondrial DNA-STING-NF-kappaB Axis-mediated microglia activation by cryptotanshinone alleviates ischemic retinopathy.
authors: Qiu, Wanlu; Zheng, Zhihua; Wang, Jiaojiao; Cai, Youran; Zou, Jiami; Huang, Ziqing; Yang, Pinglian; Ye, Weile; Jin, Mei; Zhang, Dongmei; Little, Peter J; Zhou, Qing; Liu, Zhiping
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究隐丹参酮通过抑制mtDNA-STING-NF-kB通路缓解缺血性视网膜病变，核心为小分子-蛋白互作与疾病机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic retinopathy, a leading cause of vision impairment, involves oxidative stress and dysregulated inflammation, with microglia playing a key role. Cryptotanshinone (CTS), a bioactive compound from Salvia miltiorrhiza, exhibits anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties and thus has the potential for development as a therapeutic agent. However, the actual mechanism of action of CTS in ischemic retinopathy is not known. Overactivation of the STING pathway in microglia is critical in ischemic retinopathy pathogenesis and a potential target of CTS. PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore whether CTS alleviates ischemic retinopathy by modulating microglial STING signaling. METHODS: Oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) mice and hypoxia-induced microglial cells were used. CTS efficacy in ischemic retinopathy was evaluated at multiple stages using fluorescein fundus angiography, electroretinogram, H&E staining, and Western blotting of relevant proteins. Network pharmacology and RNA sequencing identified STING as a key target. Furthermore, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), molecular docking, and site-directed mutagenesis were systematically employed to elucidate the precise binding interface between CTS and the STING protein. STING activation and knockout models were employed to further investigate the mechanisms of action of CTS. RESULTS: CTS treatment reduced microglial activation and pathological retinal angiogenesis, and protected both retinal function and structure in OIR mice. Network pharmacology, RNA sequencing, and experimental validation demonstrated a significant link between the protective effect of CTS and the inhibition of STING signaling. Mechanistically, CTS suppressed cytosolic mtDNA release, blocked STING translocation from the ER to the Golgi, and enhanced lysosomal STING degradation. These CTS-mediated effects were abolished by STING activation and absent in Sting-deficient OIR mice. Notably, CTS combined with anti-VEGF therapy showed synergistic efficacy in suppressing pathological retinal neovascularization. CONCLUSION: CTS, a natural inhibitor of STING, alleviated ischemic retinopathy by inhibiting the mtDNA-STING-NF-kappaB signaling pathway via multifaceted mechanisms in microglia.
abstract_zh: 背景：缺血性视网膜病变是视力损伤的主要原因之一，涉及氧化应激和炎症调节失调，其中小胶质细胞发挥关键作用。隐丹参酮（Cryptotanshinone, CTS）是丹参中的一种生物活性化合物，具有抗炎和抗氧化特性，因此有潜力开发为治疗药物。然而，CTS在缺血性视网膜病变中的实际作用机制尚不清楚。小胶质细胞中STING通路的过度激活在缺血性视网膜病变发病机制中至关重要，是CTS的潜在靶点。目的：本研究旨在探讨CTS是否通过调节小胶质细胞STING信号通路来缓解缺血性视网膜病变。方法：使用氧诱导视网膜病变（OIR）小鼠和缺氧诱导的小胶质细胞。通过荧光素眼底血管造影、视网膜电图、H&E染色及相关蛋白的Western blotting，在多个阶段评估CTS对缺血性视网膜病变的疗效。网络药理学和RNA测序确定STING为关键靶点。此外，系统采用表面等离子体共振（SPR）、分子对接和定点突变技术，阐明CTS与STING蛋白之间的精确结合界面。采用STING激活和敲除模型进一步研究CTS的作用机制。结果：CTS治疗减少了OIR小鼠的小胶质细胞激活和病理性视网膜血管生成，并保护了视网膜功能和结构。网络药理学、RNA测序和实验验证表明，CTS的保护作用与STING信号通路抑制之间存在显著关联。机制上，CTS抑制胞质mtDNA释放，阻断STING从内质网向高尔基体的转位，并增强溶酶体对STING的降解。这些CTS介导的效应在STING激活时被消除，在Sting缺陷的OIR小鼠中缺失。值得注意的是，CTS与抗VEGF疗法联合使用在抑制病理性视网膜新生血管方面显示出协同效应。结论：CTS作为STING的天然抑制剂，通过多方面的机制抑制小胶质细胞中的mtDNA-STING-NF-kappaB信号通路，从而缓解缺血性视网膜病变。
